learning_goal: Name the three layers of the flexor compartment, say what each muscle moves, and tell flexor digitorum superficialis from profundus by the phalanx its tendon ends on.

structures.name: right humerus
structures.label: Humerus
structures.narration: Most of this compartment starts on one small bump: the medial epicondyle.

structures.name: right radius
structures.label: Radius
structures.narration: The lateral bone. It rotates over the ulna in pronation.

structures.name: right ulna
structures.label: Ulna
structures.narration: The medial bone. It stays still while the radius turns.

structures.name: interosseous membrane of right forearm
structures.label: Interosseous membrane
structures.narration: The sheet between radius and ulna. It is what makes the forearm two compartments rather than one space, its fibres run downwards and medially from radius to ulna so that force landing on the hand is carried up to the ulna and the elbow, and both deep muscle layers take origin from it.

structures.name: right third metacarpal bone
structures.label: Third metacarpal
structures.narration: The middle finger ray — the line the long flexor tendons follow into the hand.

structures.name: middle phalanx of right middle finger
structures.label: Middle phalanx
structures.narration: Superficialis stops here. That is why it bends the PIP joint and nothing beyond it.

structures.name: distal phalanx of right middle finger
structures.label: Distal phalanx
structures.narration: Profundus goes all the way here. It is the only muscle that bends the DIP joint.

structures.name: proximal phalanx of right index finger
structures.label: Proximal phalanx (index finger)
structures.narration: The tendons run over the front of this bone on their way out to the tip; nothing in this compartment ends here.

structures.name: middle phalanx of right index finger
structures.label: Middle phalanx (index finger)
structures.narration: Superficialis stops here on this finger too. Same rule on every digit: middle phalanx, PIP joint.

structures.name: distal phalanx of right index finger
structures.label: Distal phalanx (index finger)
structures.narration: Profundus runs on past superficialis to end here. Same rule on every digit: distal phalanx, DIP joint.

structures.name: proximal phalanx of right ring finger
structures.label: Proximal phalanx (ring finger)
structures.narration: The tendons run over the front of this bone on their way out to the tip; nothing in this compartment ends here.

structures.name: middle phalanx of right ring finger
structures.label: Middle phalanx (ring finger)
structures.narration: Superficialis stops here on this finger too. Same rule on every digit: middle phalanx, PIP joint.

structures.name: distal phalanx of right ring finger
structures.label: Distal phalanx (ring finger)
structures.narration: Profundus runs on past superficialis to end here. Same rule on every digit: distal phalanx, DIP joint.

structures.name: proximal phalanx of right little finger
structures.label: Proximal phalanx (little finger)
structures.narration: The tendons run over the front of this bone on their way out to the tip; nothing in this compartment ends here.

structures.name: middle phalanx of right little finger
structures.label: Middle phalanx (little finger)
structures.narration: Superficialis stops here on this finger too. Same rule on every digit: middle phalanx, PIP joint.

structures.name: distal phalanx of right little finger
structures.label: Distal phalanx (little finger)
structures.narration: Profundus runs on past superficialis to end here. Same rule on every digit: distal phalanx, DIP joint.

structures.name: flexor retinaculum of right wrist
structures.label: Flexor retinaculum
structures.narration: A tough band across the front of the wrist. The long flexor tendons pass under it.

structures.name: humeral head of right pronator teres
structures.label: Pronator teres — humeral head
structures.narration: From the medial epicondyle. It is the most lateral of the superficial group and forms the medial border of the cubital fossa.

structures.name: ulnar head of right pronator teres
structures.label: Pronator teres — ulnar head
structures.narration: From the coronoid process of the ulna. The median nerve runs between the two heads — the site of pronator syndrome.

structures.name: right flexor carpi radialis
structures.label: Flexor carpi radialis
structures.narration: Runs to the base of the second metacarpal. Its tendon is the landmark you feel the radial pulse just lateral to.

structures.name: right palmaris longus
structures.label: Palmaris longus
structures.narration: The thin one in the middle. Absent in about one person in seven, and the one surgeons harvest for grafts.

structures.name: humeral head of right flexor carpi ulnaris
structures.label: Flexor carpi ulnaris — humeral head
structures.narration: From the medial epicondyle, like the rest of the superficial group.

structures.name: ulnar head of right flexor carpi ulnaris
structures.label: Flexor carpi ulnaris — ulnar head
terms: ulnar head of flexor carpi ulnaris
structures.narration: From the olecranon and the back of the ulna. The ulnar nerve enters the forearm between the two heads.

structures.name: humeroulnar head of right flexor digitorum superficialis
structures.label: Flexor digitorum superficialis — humeroulnar head
structures.narration: The middle layer sits by itself, deep to the four superficial muscles and superficial to the deep three.

structures.name: radial head of right flexor digitorum superficialis
structures.label: Flexor digitorum superficialis — radial head
terms: radial head of flexor digitorum superficialis
structures.narration: The two heads arch over the median nerve and ulnar artery as they enter the forearm.

structures.name: right flexor digitorum profundus
structures.label: Flexor digitorum profundus
structures.narration: The only muscle that flexes the distal interphalangeal joints. Its tendons pierce those of superficialis on the way.

structures.name: right flexor pollicis longus
structures.label: Flexor pollicis longus
structures.narration: Bends the thumb at its interphalangeal joint. Supplied by the anterior interosseous nerve.

structures.name: right pronator quadratus
structures.label: Pronator quadratus
structures.narration: A flat square across the front of the distal forearm. It is the prime pronator; pronator teres joins in when speed or force is needed.

views.title: See it in the body
views.narration: The flexor compartment is the front of the forearm. Everything here bends the wrist or the fingers, or turns the palm down.

views.title: Layer one: the superficial four
views.narration: Four superficial muscles, all from the medial epicondyle. Lateral to medial: pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris.

views.title: Layer two: superficialis alone
views.narration: Take the four off and one muscle is left in the middle layer: flexor digitorum superficialis, with a humeroulnar head and a radial head.

views.title: Layer three: the deep three
views.narration: Three deep muscles lie straight on the bones: profundus on the ulna, flexor pollicis longus on the radius, pronator quadratus across both at the wrist.

views.title: Cut across the forearm
views.narration: In cross-section the three layers stack front to back, with radius and ulna behind them. Learn the compartment as layers and the cross-section reads itself.

views.title: Radial versus ulnar pull
views.narration: Both flex the wrist. Flexor carpi radialis also pulls it to the thumb side, flexor carpi ulnaris to the little finger side. Together they flex straight.

views.title: Superficialis versus profundus
views.narration: The whole difference is where the tendon stops. Superficialis ends on the middle phalanx and bends the PIP joint. Profundus runs past it to the distal phalanx and bends the DIP joint. The same pair of insertions repeats on the index, middle, ring and little fingers — all four are drawn here, so you can see it is a rule and not a feature of one digit. Hold the other fingers straight and ask the patient to bend one — that is how you test each.

views.title: Follow profundus into the hand
views.narration: From the upper ulna, down the forearm, under the flexor retinaculum, along the finger, to the distal phalanx. One muscle belly, four long tendons — and the other three are traced here beside the middle finger, to the index, ring and little fingers, because a single belly pulling four tendons is why you cannot bend one distal joint on its own.

views.title: Lift the retinaculum
views.narration: Take the retinaculum away and the long flexor tendons are exposed where they crowd through the wrist. That crowded space is the carpal tunnel, and the median nerve is in there with them.

views.title: Turning the palm down
views.narration: Both pronators grip the radius and swing it across the ulna. Pronator quadratus works every time; pronator teres is added for power.

gaps: The catalog holds no nerve or artery meshes for the upper limb, so the median nerve between the heads of pronator teres, the ulnar nerve between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris, and the radial and ulnar arteries are taught in narration only. Nerve supply — median nerve to everything here except flexor carpi ulnaris and the ulnar half of profundus — cannot be shown as a structure.

Pronator teres, flexor carpi ulnaris and flexor digitorum superficialis have no whole-muscle mesh; each is authored from its two heads, which is anatomically finer and teaches the nerve relationships better, but a student list will show two entries per muscle.

There is no mesh for the common flexor origin, the bicipital aponeurosis or the antebrachial fascia, so those attachments are described rather than shown. The interosseous membrane is NOT missing — FMA23707 is in the catalog and is authored as a part of the Radius & ulna scene — and it is the boundary this compartment is defined by, so it should be added here.

All four fingers reached by the long flexor tendons are now drawn as proximal, middle and distal phalanges (FMA24451/24455/24460 index, FMA24452/24456/24461 middle, FMA24453/24457/24462 ring, FMA24454/24458/24463 little), so the four-tendon fan is shown rather than described. Of the six newly added, only the three proximal phalanges are in the local mesh set today; the middle and distal phalanges of index, ring and little finger (FMA24455, FMA24460, FMA24457, FMA24462, FMA24458, FMA24463) are catalogued but not yet fetched, so until they are, beat 7's insertion pairs and beat 8's fan traces render on the middle finger only.
